statements.status_notes: PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-6474 (PostgreSQL timeofday() can disclose portions of server memory) in 16.14 on the PostgreSQL 16 branch: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-6474/ lists 16.14 as the fixed release for major version 16 (versions before 16.14 are affected), and the 16.14 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.14/, list this CVE. The fix is commits https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/24e0e32544c3664447555eda8f56c4e0fffcdaa4 (src/backend/utils/adt/timestamp.c: timeofday() no longer passes text produced by pg_strftime() to snprintf() as a format string) and https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/79b7847c729bcbbe7ae2af1742adc6db86904932 (src/timezone/strftime.c) on the REL_16_STABLE branch; both are tagged Security: CVE-2026-6474 and are in the REL_16_14 release tag and not in REL_16_13. The DHI postgresql16 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; the 16.14-r0 APKBUILD, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/56de254843f841a99aedea4953a2dc9ec9338eb4/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD, differs from the 16.13-r0 one only in the version and tarball checksum, applies no patch that touches the files this fix changes, and lists CVE-2026-6474 under its 16.14-r0 secfixes. We checked the postgres server binary, /usr/libexec/postgresql16/postgres, in every postgresql16 build published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI package repository as of 2026-11-27, on both x86_64 and aarch64 (package checksums verified against the package index): 16.13-r0 reports PostgreSQL 16.13 and is affected, while 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0 report 16.14, 16.15 and 16.16 and carry the fix. As a check, the server binary in 16.13-r0 contains the old combined timeofday() format string ('%a %b %d %H:%M:%S.%%06d %Y %Z') that the fix removes, and 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0 instead contain the split format strings it adds, on both architectures. 16.14-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.
